```plato
//==
// # Curves
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - ICurve interfaces
//  - ICurve capability interfaces

//==
// # ICurve interfaces
//
// Continuous curves as pure functions: a curve maps one parameter to a position
// (the IProcedural interface from `functional.concepts.plato`). Unless a type
// documents otherwise, the canonical parameter domain of a curve is the unit
// interval [0,1], and closed curves satisfy Eval(0) = Eval(1). The optional
// capabilities a curve may add on top — derivatives, moving frames, polar form,
// periodicity, arc-length measurement — are declared in the next section.
// See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICurve.

//==
// # Curves

// A continuous map from one real parameter to a value of TRange: the generic
// root of every curve. Dimension-agnostic curve helpers constrain on this, so
// an Eval-only derivation is written once instead of once per embedding
// (see `Sample` in curves.library.plato). Mirrors the
// `IField<TDomain, TValue>` root of `fields.concepts.plato`.
interface ICurve<TRange>
    inherits IProcedural<Number, TRange>
{ }
```
